advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _pinned_replacement_target iterate all 'duplicates' deps for a usable target and fall through to the 'supersedes' inbound pass, matching replacement_of(require_live=True).
evidence: close_scope.py:66-72: `for dep in state.get("deps") or []: if dep.get("relation") == "duplicates": return _live_pinned_ticket(...)` — returns unconditionally on first duplicates dep
close_disposition.py:126-131: replacement_of loops all deps and only `return target` when `_usable(target)`, otherwise continues to the inbound supersedes pass at 139-144
docstring claims parity: close_scope.py:64 `"""Pinned-view equivalent of ``replacement_of(..., require_live=True)``."""`
advisory.finding: _pinned_replacement_target diverges from replacement_of(require_live=True): it returns on the FIRST 'duplicates' dep and yields None if that single target isn't live, whereas replacement_of iterates all 'duplicates' deps for a usable one and only then falls through to the 'supersedes' inbound pass. In the pinned/billable-verifier path a live replacement reachable via a second duplicate link or via supersedes (when a non-live duplicate link exists) is missed, so the parent close can fail to be credited where the non-pinned path would credit it.
scenarios: A ticket carries a stale/archived 'duplicates' link plus a live 'supersedes' inbound link — non-pinned path credits the live replacement, pinned path returns None.
A ticket has two 'duplicates' links where the first target is archived and the second is live.
advisory.suggested_fix: Loop duplicates deps, continue when _live_pinned_ticket returns None, and only after exhausting duplicates check inbound supersedes links.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the pinned-view show_ticket calls in the disposition-expansion path so an unresolvable/unreadable sibling degrades consistently with the non-pinned branch.
evidence: close_scope.py:47-50 (non-pinned) `try: state = reduce_ticket(...) except Exception: return None`
close_scope.py:39 `state = ticket_view.show_ticket(ticket_id)` — no guard
close_scope.py:82 `state = ticket_view.show_ticket(resolved)` — no guard
ticket_view.py:216-219 show_ticket raises PinnedTicketNotFound when resolve returns None
advisory.finding: The pinned branch of replacement_target_for_closed_disposition and _pinned_replacement_target/_live_pinned_ticket call ticket_view.show_ticket unguarded, unlike the non-pinned branch which wraps reduce_ticket in try/except to fail-closed on unreadable/malformed siblings. A ticket_view.show_ticket raising (e.g. PinnedTicketNotFound or other PinnedTicketViewError) propagates and aborts the whole precheck rather than degrading like the non-pinned path.
scenarios: An id in accepted_ids (or a replacement descendant) is not resolvable at the pinned tracker revision, or the pinned object read errors.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the `not state.get('error')` guard to _live_pinned_ticket to match _is_live_ticket's liveness definition.
evidence: close_scope.py:83 `if state.get("archived") or state.get("status") in {"archived", "deleted"}: return None` — no error check
close_precheck.py:38-43 _is_live_ticket: `not state.get("error") and not state.get("archived") and state.get("status") not in {"archived","deleted"}`
advisory.finding: _live_pinned_ticket omits the `not state.get('error')` liveness check that _is_live_ticket applies, so a pinned replacement whose reduced state carries an error field but lacks 'archived'/status in {archived,deleted} is treated as a live replacement in the pinned path but not in the non-pinned path.
scenarios: A replacement ticket reduces to an error/degraded state at the pinned revision.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where a duplicate/superseded child names a replacement whose subtree carries NO referencing commit, asserting the epic close still raises RebarError with the 'no commit references it' / file_impact message and stays in_progress.
evidence: close_scope.py:20-23 docstring: 'only a ticket already closed with a close class and naming a live replacement can add that replacement, and the ordinary no-reference failure still fires when the expanded scope contains no commit.'
Ticket 9181 AC3: 'The fix preserves the current protection: a code-impact ticket with no referencing commit in its accepted evidence set still fails with `cannot confirm the work landed`.'

The only new positive test test_parent_close_credits_duplicate_child_replacement_commit commits a trailer against the replacement (_commit_ref(rebar_repo, replacement)); there is no companion test where the expanded scope (replacement + its descendants) contains zero referencing commits and the epic close must still raise RebarError.

ABSENCE: the held-out companion tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_subtree_heldout.py pins only the prior ferric-jet-scorpion/1edf subtree cases (grandchild transitivity, no-subtree-commit block, leaf no-regression) and does not close over disposition replacements added by this diff.
advisory.finding: The new no-reference fail-closed contract for the disposition-expansion path is untested: no test exercises a parent whose only duplicate/superseded child names a replacement that itself carries NO referencing commit anywhere in its subtree, so the promised 'still fails closed for missing work' behavior (docstring lines 22-23; ticket AC3) is not regression-guarded.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add test_parent_close_still_blocks_when_replacement_has_no_commit: build epic -> duplicate_child(file_impact) linked 'duplicates' to a replacement(file_impact) that is closed with NO _commit_ref, then assert pytest.raises(rebar.RebarError) on _close(epic) with 'file_impact'/'commit' in stderr and status still 'in_progress'.
